Aonde, adonde. “Y onde no yegue ey sentío, —yegará la boluntá.” , p. 138. “Esoj seloj de tu amante —Me dan ganaj de reil. —Pobresito del que pasa —Por onde han pasao mil.” Cantar popular. Valle Atiles, El campesino, 1888. (Es del antiguo español. “Quiero saber, reyna, onde es vuestra andada.” Libro de Alexandre, verso 1720. Es corriente entre los judeos españoles. “Ni onde tu tía vayas cada día.” “Onde entra el beber, sale el saber.” “Onde irás, amigos toparás.” RHi., 1895, 2, 336). 1.en_consolidated_definition: where, whither. "And where I have not been, —there my will shall be." (p. 138). "That is the way of your lover —It gives me a pang of regret. —Poor wretch who passes by —Where so many have passed." Popular song. Valle Atiles, El campesino, 1888. (From old Spanish. "I want to know, queen, where your journey has taken you." Book of Alexandre, verse 1720. It is common among Spanish Jews. "Neither where your aunt goes every day." "Where drinking begins, knowledge emerges." "Where you go, you will meet friends." RHi., 1895, 2, 336). (It persists in colloquial speech: "I climb the difficult slope; —tired and exhausted I come. —I cannot take my eyes —from where my thoughts are." Alonso Cortés, Cantares de Castilla, núm. 1580, RHi., 1914, 32, 204).
